limits: Python and libraries on this page: the page's own playground runs in your browser, in Python 3.13.2, while the research ran Python 3.14.6 on Linux with PyAutoGUI 0.9.54, PyScreeze 1.0.1, PyMsgBox 2.0.1, Pillow 12.3.0, NumPy 2.5.4, OpenCV 5.0.0.93 and pyperclip 1.11.0 (and other releases where a section says so).

Recorded, not run: all 74 examples of the chapter. A browser's Python (its platform is 'emscripten') has no mouse or keyboard to control, no X server, no PyAutoGUI backend and cannot start the programs the examples need (Xvfb, child interpreters, windows); each example is shown with its output recorded under Python 3.14.6, labelled 'Recorded, not run on this page', with its reason: BackendSources, BadKeyName, CaptchaEthics, ClickButtons, ClickSequence, ClipboardRoundTrip, ColorDepth, DoubleAndTriple, DragEvents, DragVersusMove, DurationSteps, ExactMatchAndConfidence, FailsafeCorners, FailsafeFires, FailsafePointsFixed, FailsafeSlam, FocusDecides, HoldContext, HotkeyOrder, IdleResets, ImageNotFound, InvalidEscape, KeyAliases, KeyNameList, KeyTable, KeyboardLayout, LibraryVersion, LocateAllAndClick, LocateBox, LocateWaits, LogoutHotkeys, LookingBusy, MacAccessibility, MessageBoxResults, MessageBoxTimeout, MouseInfoNoDelay, MouseInfoTk9, MouseInfoWindow, MoveRelative, NoDisplayImport, NoVersionOne, OldScreezeReturnsNone, OriginAndCorners, OutOfRange, PauseDefault, PixelColor, PixelMatch, PositionTuple, PracticeAnswers, PyMsgBoxReleases, PythonTargets, ScalingMismatch, ScreenSize, ScreenshotImage, ScreenshotNeedsScrot, ScrollEvents, ScrollUnits, ShadowedName, ShiftFour, ShippedSpiralDraw, SleepAndCountdown, SpiralDrawing, SushiGoRound, SyntheticVersusReal, TkVersions, TwoVirtualMonitors, WaylandSession, WindowAttributes, WindowFunctionsLinux, WindowsSendInput, WriteInterval, WriteString, XTestEvents, XtermIgnoresSent.

Virtual display, not a real screen: every recorded program that moves the mouse, clicks, types, scrolls or reads the screen ran against a private virtual X display (Xvfb) with real X clients, a local stand-in for a screen; the events were seen there and nobody saw the screen. Nothing ran on Windows or macOS, on a real Wayland compositor, on a real or second monitor or with HiDPI scaling.

Pictures: 6 recorded pictures drawn or captured by the research programs on that virtual display (under LocateBox, MouseInfoWindow, ScreenshotImage, SpiralDrawing, WindowAttributes, WriteString) are shown beside their examples, labelled 'Recorded picture, not made on this page'; they are SHA-256 checked when the page is made.

No wheel is embedded on this page and no file of the book's online materials (a zip of 7,759,877 bytes holding 91 files; spiralDraw.py is the one that uses PyAutoGUI). The licence of the zip and of its files is an open question for the owner (03-materials/ch23/assets/ASSETS_PROVENANCE_v1_0_0.md).

NOT EXECUTED: Windows (SendInput, UIPI, the window objects of PyGetWindow, the logout hotkey) and macOS (Quartz, the accessibility permission, the logout hotkey); a real Wayland compositor; real or several monitors and HiDPI scaling; applications that block synthetic input; a real instant messenger; the Sushi Go Round game and a captcha; the final Python 3.15 (uv offered 3.15.0b4); Python 3.11 with Tk; the commit the course pins; and a photograph (the single request to Wikimedia Commons answered 429).
